Hi Alex —

Thanks for sending this over. I started a draft of Section A and attached it (kimberly_ssq_draft.pdf). High-level notes up front:

- PII classification: we label fields at ingestion using customer-configurable classifiers; default classifier flags common identifiers (email, SSN, phone) and user-provided schema can add fields.
- Pseudonymization: for hosted/Dedicated, we support prefix redaction and optional tokenization at the proxy layer before it reaches the model when customers opt-in.
- Subprocessors: the runtime uses select GPU infra providers and analytics partners; we will provide an up-to-date subprocessor roster and per-subprocessor visibility mapping.
- KV cache: session KV cache is encrypted at rest and scoped to the customer tenant; default retention is 6 hours after last access, configurable per-customer with a max of 30 days.
- Cross-border & KMS: customers can bring their own KMS (BYOK) for key custody in Private and Dedicated; hosted customers are served from region-specific KMS with documented transfer controls.

I want the engineering team to confirm a couple of specific items (see inline comments in the attached draft):
1) precise KV eviction semantics for long-running streaming sessions
2) whether our analytics exporter strips identifiers by default or uses a hashed identifier with salt

Marissa / Priyom / Aditya — can you review the draft and the inline comments? If we can finalize this afternoon we can book a walkthrough with Alex for tomorrow morning.

Kimberly — quick technical clarifications below, pulling from runtime & infra owners (copied answers kept short):

> KV cache retention & eviction
- KV is segmented per-tenant, encrypted with tenant-specific envelope keys. Eviction is LRU with a pinned-token mechanism for in-progress streams; long-running streams maintain pinned slots for up to 48 hours before moving to cold storage (encrypted) which is purged per tenant retention policy.

> Analytics exporter identifiers
- Exporter emits only a salted hash of identifiers by default. The salt is rotated monthly; analytics partners receive only the hashed value unless a customer explicitly requests raw identifiers through a contract addendum.

> Subprocessors list & visibility
- Current subprocessors: CloudGPU (in-region compute partner), FastLogs (observability exporter), VaultKey (managed KMS for hosted), and PartnerWrap (model tuning). We will generate a per-subprocessor matrix showing what data each subprocessor can access (raw/pseudonymized/hashed).

> Diagram link
- Updated dataflow with redaction points: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-redwood-healthsync-ssq (redwood_dataflow_v2.png)

I'll also attach a concise runbook excerpt for deletion APIs and audit log evidence. Will follow up with Marissa on policy mapping for the DPA section.

- Subprocessor visibility: will provide matrix with columns {access_type, data_scope, location, SOC2 status}.
- KMS custody: BYOK available for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses regional VaultKey with restricted export.
- Retention & deletion: deletion API available (sync job + audit log) and documented in the runbook; default KV retention 6 hours, configurable to 30 days; long-running streams pinned up to 48 hours then cold-purged per tenant policy.
